channel noun

for water

also canal, water channel, conduit, irrigation channel, watercourse

classical

Caes. BC 2.10; Liv. 23.31.9; Vitr. 8.6 (Lewis & Short)
Verg. G. 3.330 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 289

canālis, canālis m.

noun, third declension

a channel, a conduit, a pipe; a canal

Any pipe or channel, open or closed, especially for water; rarely feminine in Cato and Varro (Lewis & Short). The modern languages use it for a television channel, which here is statiō (see channel).

Other words

  • rīvus, rīvī m. — a brook; a channel for irrigation

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Verg. Ecl. 3.111

    A small stream, natural or led off by hand to water the fields.

  • fossa, fossae f. — a ditch, a dug channel, a canal

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 203; Traupman 286

    Anything dug, from a ditch to a canal (see trench).

Examples

  • Claudite jam rīvōs, puerī; sat prāta bibērunt.

    Close the channels now, boys: the meadows have drunk enough.Verg. Ecl. 3.111

See also channel, trench, stream, river, gutter.
